$comment: Operator decision log (scripts/analysis/decision-log.mjs; Spec 124 R-HK). Imported verbatim from the committed chat record docs/reports/decisions/raw/2026-11-03-batch-ax/2026-11-03-batch-ax.json. `decision_vocab`, `routing` (the register and row that record each decision), `amendments` and `options` are added by the lane and are not the operator's text; everything else is re-derived from `source.raw` by `--check`.

decisions.question: M-465: Roof form is a labelled design option in Phase 2 (M-400's first option): `height_m`, `main_wall_height_m` and `upper_storey_setback_m` are stored for a flat or shallow roof and for a pitched roof, with the clause's own flat-or-shallow threshold beside them; Layer 3 headlines the larger.
decisions.recommendation: Operator answer (~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/inc2/open-questions.md): "definitely option A", "OP-1 confirmed", "0-A-a", "step-back approved. ggo work with this one". Rule text: (1) **The option.** Phase 2 resolves every target of a Layer 1 unit whose condition carries `flat_or_shallow_roof` once with the token held ("flat or shallow roof") and once not held ("pitched roof"), and stores both rows labelled, keyed by option like class (M-400). The row without an option stays the M-60 answer. (2) **Share the cell.** Where the two worlds agree, an option row is the closed code `shared` and reads the row without an option; only where they differ are the two answers stored in full. (3) **Pitched step-back.** "A target whose by-law value units on the lot are all out **only because** a condition token declared in `vocab.design_options` is false (`applies()` returns `ok: false` with the false condition being that token, for the run's design option) **does not apply**. The result is `not_applicable:<the first such unit's clause, in candidate order>`, never `not_evaluated:no_candidate`. A unit out for any other reason (another false condition, a building type, a DISAPPLY) keeps today's rules. A token outside `design_options` is unchanged; `major_street` (Q-KG3, M-346) and every `absence_ignore` list stay as they are. An undecided token (no option set) is never false, so the row without an option is unchanged. Layer 3 reads it as no cap, as for M-183(2)." So a pitched `upper_storey_setback_m` is `not_applicable:<the zone's flat-roof clause>` (M-218's note "a pitched roof gets no step-back"; LC-54 (131:104)). (4) **The threshold.** `pitched_roof_slope_min` (ratio) is stored beside the option rows, generated per clause from the clause's own words: 0.1 where the clause reads "less than 1.0 vertical units for every 10.0 horizontal units". The 1:4 clauses of the 29 RD exceptions are keyed by the MB-27.L2 1:4 sub-task (CARD-1in4-rekey); until then they keep their existing keying, disclosed. A clause that reads only "flat roof" generates no threshold; the lot takes the zone's 1:10 (reading (i) of that card). The lot takes its strictest clause, and the value is never a Layer 3 setting (OP-1, M-376, M-387). (5) **Share caps.** The share caps apply on each roof row where `main_wall_height_m` is a number; elsewhere they are not applicable. (6) **Class.** "Increment 2 stores the roof option and its threshold for the detached house class; another building type's roof option is resolved and stored when its increment needs it, by a pin change and its own Layer 2 night. Until then, Layer 3 answers `not_modelled` for it (R3-11)." (7) **Storage** is measured against the 0.60 ratio, which is held; the line is never raised. The M-172(3) class move: a design-choice token declared in `vocab.design_options` is resolved per option (M-400); M-172(3)'s "taken as met" and "restrictive trade-off" do not apply to it; like a scenario-filled (M-160) token it is filled by the run's option, never by data or a default; its phrase stays in `design_choice_disclosure.lot_condition` as the option's label and it has no `default_overrides` entry (the 2026-10-29 note: "each result is shown labelled with its option; no option is chosen silently"). Spec 134 I13: I13's legal `needs_user_input` axes lose `roof_type` (a design option, not a legal user input); no option row carries `condition_unknown:<its option token>`; this is counted in `scenario_axis_cells`; Spec 134 §3: option and threshold slots are appended after the base pairs and read through `bylaw_resolution_option_results`; `bylaw_resolution_results` keeps its key and its 54 pairs. LC-67: LC-67 (131:117) "only where `main_wall_height_m` is a number" is applied per roof row; R3-01 (M-385) carries a not_evaluated only where a roof row's own wall limit is not evaluated. (The three `{L2-...}` paragraphs are lane E's v2 §8 text, summarised here; paste verbatim at record time.)

decisions.question: M-480: The Layer 3 grammar gains three forms, `refuse(<reason>)`, `flag(<word>; <expr>)` and `best_of(<rows>; ceiling: <expr>)`, plus the reason word `pitched_form_not_offered` and the interim flag `headline_lower_bound: main_wall_shares_not_resolved` (dated note on M-72, as a row because M-72 sits in the frozen M19 block, the M-377 form).
decisions.recommendation: Operator answer (~/Buildo-scratch/p2close/CARD-l3-schema-forms.md): "3-F1 approved", "approved provided that itts complaint". Rule text: M-72's closed Layer 3 grammar gains three forms, Layer 3 only (Layer 1 is unchanged). (1) `refuse(<reason word>)` returns `not_evaluated:<reason word>`, where the word is from the closed reason list (M-64); for example `if(half_span_a_m > lv(rafter_span_4_m); refuse(no_cited_rafter_span); <selector>)`. (2) `flag(<word>; <expr>)` returns the value of `<expr>` with the disclosure word added to its flags (R3-02 carries it onward); for example `if(<plate> ≤ 0 m2; flag(setback_storey_not_built; 0 m2); <plate>)`. (3) `best_of(<row>; <row>; …; ceiling: <expr>)` returns the largest evaluated candidate. A tie goes to the first in argument order, never sorted, and the result carries the flag `headline:<row id>`. Each not_evaluated candidate adds `headline_lower_bound:<row id>`, except a candidate whose reason is an R3-05 drop reason (`pitched_form_not_offered`, or an option Phase 2 refuses): it is dropped with its reason and raises no lower bound. No lower-bound flag is raised when the result equals `ceiling` (a missing form cannot exceed it). If every candidate is not_evaluated, it returns the first one's reason. Its flags: the result keeps every flag of the winning candidate, plus `headline:<row id>` and the drop and lower-bound flags, and never a losing candidate's own flags (so a lower bound or a disclosure that belongs to a loser is never shown as the headline's). The closed reason list gains `pitched_form_not_offered`: the steepest pitch that fits is below the clause's flat-or-shallow threshold (M-461, OP-1), so no pitched form exists on that lot (an R3-05 drop reason). Until M-471's Phase 2 lock lands, wherever the flat form is the headline below its caps it carries `headline_lower_bound: main_wall_shares_not_resolved`, with no lot flag and no zone test in Layer 3; after that, the existing `regulated()` splits it. All three forms are built red-first as one item, before increment 2's rounds and before the roof-axis night. It moves `evaluator_version`; its version re-pins are named approvals at landing. No other form is added.
decisions.operator_quote: 3-F1 approved; approved provided that itts complaint

Every result shows the confidence beside each reading it rests on: each reading switch on its path is listed with its confidence (M-378: "every result lists the switches on its path"). It covers the increment-2 readings, and the increment-3 readings when their rows are authored. The switchboard schema and its lock change by this ruling (Process 1). It is built red-first, together with the M-72 forms build; there is no Layer 2 rule change and no night; the Layer 3 step goldens (the 25) are recaptured with explained diffs; its version re-pins are named approvals at landing. ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/CONFIDENCE-REGISTER.md becomes a view of the switchboard once built.
